title: Enforce simple scatter supports at opt-in checker and exporter boundaries
body:
PR2977 demonstrated that `scatter[0] += [0,0]` passes the selected full symbolic checker but exports an extra ADD. This opt-in successor adopts `simple-scatter-v1` and enforces the same simple-support validator before both checker and exporter execution. It snapshots the validated word and authenticated delegate script before running the unchanged source, so replacing the original input path cannot bypass the guard.

The selected word produces all three original artifacts byte for byte (27,234 records); a separate scalar F2 interpreter checks all 661 arbitrary-input columns. Both entry modes reject the paired mutant before output creation, while existing-output and semantic-failure controls retain the promised boundary. Export mode validates the schema only; it does not replace full symbolic/native checking.

Validation passed locally:
- Registered package replay on CPython 3.12.14, including nine behavioral groups.
- Primary replay and all nine groups under CPython 3.14.7 with `-I -O -Werror -B`.
- All 364 ordered rows of length <=5 over three indices, with all eight copied-bit assignments on accepted supports; malformed types, odd/even duplicates, reordered rows, input replacement, source corruption, omitted ADD and truncated-record controls.
- Metadata/source pins, whitespace and exact publication-byte preflight (13 package/input files).

Sources and task are pinned at canonical main `836b19bfa309ceafbc8ee32a15e8c4b10dde7e11`, priority revision 6. The accepted draw was bit mechanisms; TASK.json explicitly records the change from `bit-helper-contract` to the revision-6/PR2977 boundary handoff. Final overlap coverage: 234 open PRs, 2,440 closed PRs and 1,703 discussion records, complete pagination and no warnings; sparse local-note/diff coverage remains a limitation.

This completes a local successor boundary module, not selected-supplier adoption. Frozen sources, manifests and the selected frontier are unchanged. Native compilation, complete selected cold replay, hosting/precision and all-size admission were not run; hosted CI is separate.

Credit Nick Petalas / PR2977 (`cd23d242dfe0e7a71cafba0ad5590dc4f2fbf4f2`) for the counterexample, candidate guard and handoff; eumemic, DreamingOfClouds, Dylan Crow and Douglas Colkitt retain the source-lineage credit detailed in the README. Prepared for Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0, no independent human review claimed. [Canonical investigation and claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2976#discussioncomment-18977810).
